title: An asymptotic formula for the number of totients
main_claim: V(x) ~ (x/log x) G_m A(1;theta), where G_m is Ford's simplex scale and A(1;.) is a uniform limit of explicit finite inclusion-exclusion coefficients A_H, bounded above and away from zero. As a consequence V(cx)/V(x) -> c for every fixed c>0 (the Erdos-Hall question). A companion result gives a weighted asymptotic for N_k(x), the count of values v<=x with least preimage l(v) in (kx,(k+1)x], with a positive/zero dichotomy; the positive case is shown for k=1,2.

issues.location: extraction.tex, eq. (ford-bands)/(ford-simplex), proof of Prop. basic
issues.description: Coverage (every preimage of all but epsilon_H V(x) values is a basic witness) rests entirely on the paper's transcription of Ford's Theorems 10 and 16, including the specific slack factors xi_i = 1 + 1e-4 e^{-h_i/40}, the parameter Psi=P, and the 'some preimage fails' convention. The derivation from those statements is correct, but I could not check the cited statements against Ford's 2013 arXiv revision. If Theorem 16 has a different xi_i or a different range of Psi, the constants in Lemma boxes would have to change. The structure of the argument would not.
issues.evidence: Ford's Theorem 16, with its parameter Psi=P, states that all but O(V(x)e^{-P^2/4}) values have every preimage satisfying ... sum a_{r-i}u_r <= xi_i u_i

coverage:
I read all seven source files in build/source: introduction, statements, extraction, layers, collisions, limits and companion. Checked in detail:
(1) Prop. comparison: the top layer and the 3-form sieve. Intermediate layers in both cases (Q1=Q2 and Q1!=Q2, including the two cross-slot incidences). The allocation-entropy bound. The exponent telescoping; I verified c_{j+1}-c_j-2=a_j symbolically.
(2) Prop. collisions: factor alignment via normality, cancellation of equal indices, the reduced-index bound a_k<=a_{j_k}, the slack saving (log y)^{-1-kappa h^{-4}} against the costs exp(O(h^2)) and exp(O(b_i log h/h^8)), the dyadic sum, and the prefix restoration.
(3) Lemma finite-map and Prop. unique-prefix, including the least-preimage identity l(v)=Q l(d) and coprimality via w<p_R.
(4) Lemma simplex: the beta-scaling inclusion and the slack-marginal densities. Lemma concentration centering. Shell estimate h^{-3} summed to H^{-2}. Smooth-cofactor Rankin bound.
(5) Lemma tail-volume: the intersection volume G_R(1-q)^R, q_{m,T} -> gamma S_T/(alpha m), and G_{m-H}/G_m -> (gamma/alpha)^H rho^{H(H-1)/2}. These match the A_H formula and its exponential-variable interpretation. Tail-witness conditions match the basic-witness conditions under h=m-i.
(6) Prop. mass, the fixed-scaling corollary (exact cancellation of M_1), and the uniform-Cauchy argument in Lemma coefficient-convergence along exact-phase sequences.
(7) Companion: the interval length T f_k(r/q), the Lipschitz perturbation, the dichotomy, and the positivity argument.
Numerical checks (mpmath/sympy): rho=0.54260 (inside 0.54-0.545); 30 lambda=18.34 (between 18 and 20); 1.1 rho=0.597<0.6; C_0=0.8178146 and D_0=2.1769687 both match. For Ford's seed d=2^18*257, an inverse-totient computation gives all 8 preimages divisible by 8 and l(d)/d=2.0078>2, confirming k=1,2.
Not independently verified: the exact statements of Ford's Theorems 10 and 16, Lemma 2.6 and Section 5, and of Ford's 2023 sieve Theorem 2.5. These are taken as cited.
